clue.text: Battle later set off in court

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters sit inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: set off suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A battle is fought later on, with the action starting off inside a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb, to woo; 'set off' makes ATERL.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is the 1815 battle where Napoleon was finally defeated.

clue.text: According to Edgar after vacation, a lethal snake's encountered

indicators.note: after places the emptied name behind the snake

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, famed for killing Cleopatra

indicators.note: vacation means emptying out, so the inside of the name goes and its outer letters stay

explanation.surface: Edgar, back from holiday, reports meeting a deadly snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' reads as a holiday but means emptying the name out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a formal way of saying in accordance with, as in instructions followed to the letter.

clue.text: Dotty reveals metallic sound that doesn't stop

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters of the next word go mad and are rearranged

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound made by metal

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric uncovers a clanging noise that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' rearranges REVEALS into EVERLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting goes on forever, never coming to an end.

clue.text: Topless oblivious youth, unoccupied at work, displays dance

indicators.note: topless means the head of the word is removed; in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: blind to something means oblivious of it

indicators.note: unoccupied means emptied, leaving only the outside letters of the word

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A careless young person, idle at work, shows off a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' drops B from BLIND; 'unoccupied' empties youth to YH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lindy hop is a swing dance that originated in Harlem in the late 1920s.

clue.text: Fruit with loose stone consumed in old African territory

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit
loose means free, not tied down
st is the abbreviation for the stone, a British unit of weight
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Fruit containing a loose stone is eaten somewhere in Africa long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Free State was a nineteenth-century Boer republic, later a province of South Africa.

clue.text: Raw youngster entertains academic element

indicators.note: entertains means holds as a guest, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a colt is an inexperienced youngster, especially a young player
BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is an academic graduate

explanation.surface: An inexperienced young person plays host to a scholarly guest.
explanation.walkthrough: A colt is a young horse, and by extension a raw young player.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a hard bluish metallic chemical element, number 27.

clue.text: A few words nipper's read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud says the word is spoken, giving a different word of the same sound

parts.note: claws are a crab's nippers; the possessive heard aloud has the same sounds

explanation.surface: A short passage is recited by a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' suggests a small child, but here it is a crab's pincer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a short group of words forming part of a sentence or a contract.

clue.text: Gripped coin

definitions.meaning: past tense of bite: held tight between the teeth
a small coin, as in a threepenny piece or an American quarter, two of these

explanation.surface: Someone clutched a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bit is the past tense of bite, meaning gripped, and also a name for a small coin.

clue.text: Author that is taking shelter by meandering Ural

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the rearranged river beside the other pieces
meandering, as a river winds, signals that the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
lee means shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A writer takes refuge beside the winding Ural river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meandering' rearranges the river's letters to LAUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurie Lee was the English writer of Cider with Rosie.

clue.text: Revolutionary records in French involving electronic organ

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: en is French for in
e is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Radical recordings in French include an electronic organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' gives SPL; 'involving' wraps the French word round E.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an abdominal organ that filters blood.

clue.text: Prickly plant is unable to flourish latterly in Australia

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: can't means is unable

indicators.note: latterly points to the end of the word, so its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A spiny plant fails to thrive in the end in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latterly' takes the last letter of flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a genus of spiny-leaved plants whose leaves inspired Corinthian columns.

clue.text: Gala rarely captivating around foreign waters

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the captured letters are read backwards
captivating means holding inside, so the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A gala seldom charms people from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' takes LARA from gaLA RArely; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea is a shrinking lake in Central Asia, waters abroad from a British view.

clue.text: Split appeared in this old country

definitions.text: Split appeared in this old country

parts.words: Split appeared in this old country
parts.note: Split is a Croatian city that was part of a former Balkan federation, which itself split up

explanation.surface: A former nation in which a division appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: Split reads as a rift, but it is the Croatian port; the federation also broke apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Balkan federation included Croatia, where the city of Split lies.

clue.text: Nasa help to develop a way for this pioneer to explore

indicators.note: to develop means to change and grow, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: The space agency helps build a route for an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges NASAHELP into ALANSHEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Shepard became the first American in space in 1961, a pioneering astronaut.

clue.text: Intellectual, not popular, accepting career rejection

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other
not says the popular word is taken away

parts.note: a boffin is a clever scientist or intellectual
in means popular, fashionable
to career is to rush along

explanation.surface: An intellectual, out of favour, takes a job that turns him down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' leaves BOFF; 'career' is the verb, to hurtle along.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush-off is a curt dismissal or snub.

clue.text: Facility's head tracks study on island

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, places the first piece above the next
tracks means follows behind, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A facility's director follows a study on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility can mean ease or preparedness for action, a sense close to readiness.

clue.text: "Ten" given by the Parisian after ballerina's final pivot

indicators.note: after places the other pieces behind the dancer's final letter
final points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer's last spin earns a perfect ten from a French judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' gives A, the end of ballerina; X and LE come 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod on which a wheel turns, so a kind of pivot.

clue.text: Expert checks runner perhaps over one year — suspension's given

indicators.note: checks means restrains or holds in, so the expert surrounds the rest

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: over means covering, so the bean wraps round the year

parts.note: a runner bean is one kind of bean
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An expert inspects a sprinter after a year, and a ban is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is not an athlete but a runner bean; 'over' and 'checks' build BEYAN then the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyance is a state of temporary suspension, matters held in abeyance.

clue.text: Cheers football team vehicle

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A toast to the football team's coach.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is informal British thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Given small space, managed using type of wallpaper?

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
bossed means ordered about, managed

explanation.surface: Given a tiny room, someone ran things with some patterned wallpaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Embossed wallpaper has a raised pattern; 'type' hints at printing, where EM is a space.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossed paper has a raised relief design, a common style of decorating paper for walls.

clue.text: Bowl from opening pair of cricketers maintaining speed

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the first letters wrap round the other piece
opening pair of picks the first two letters of the word

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: Bowling from the first two batsmen keeps up the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like a cricket verb but is the noun, a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow, as on the moon.

clue.text: Bob's crying upset his Hollywood partner?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bob is crying, which upsets his partner in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers to Bob Hope, Crosby's partner in the Road films.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby starred with comedian Bob Hope in the Road to ... film series.

clue.text: English flower close to the office

indicators.note: close to means the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: a den is a private study or office

explanation.surface: An English bloom grows near the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: a river. The Eden runs through Cumbria in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eden is a river in northern England, and a river is a flower in crossword terms.

clue.text: The Andalusian's seen bending part of body

parts.note: el is Spanish for the, as spoken in Andalusia
to bow is to bend

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is seen bending part of their body.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm.

clue.text: Aide moving outside intended to avoid a complaint

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
moving means the letters shift around
to avoid means leaving out, so the following letter is dropped

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A helper on the move outside meant to dodge an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' makes DEIA; 'to avoid a' leaves MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean an illness or medical disorder, and dementia is one.

clue.text: Fish Beverly regularly rejected

indicators.note: regularly rejected means every other letter is thrown away, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A fish that Beverly keeps turning down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' tempts a reversal, but the letters B, V, R, Y are the ones thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Appreciation shown by bishop in US state neighbouring

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the state

parts.note: NY is New York
an ear, as in an ear for music, is an appreciation
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Gratitude is shown by a bishop in an American state next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby describes something close at hand, next door.

clue.text: Best man perhaps comes through role having inebriated groom

indicators.note: comes through means passes into the middle, so the saint sits inside
inebriated means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: a saint, ST, is a man at his best; perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.surface: The best man passes through his role, with a drunken groom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inebriated' turns ROLE into OLER; ST 'comes through' it. 'groom' is a stable hand, not a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler is a stableman at an inn, a groom who looks after horses.

clue.text: Media chief screening agreed particular order for contestants

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the editor surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an ed, editor, is a chief in the media
yes means agreed
own means particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A media boss covers an agreed special order for game show contestants.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the call at the start of a game of bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: The call opening a bingo game tells players to concentrate on their cards.
